_note: Predictive Sandbox R&D content. Family: pressure_system. Texture: sustained load, standoff, and strain rather than a single sharp event. Routes on semantic_state / dominant_operation / gradient as computed by engine/predictive_engine.py (_window_semantic_metrics). Deliberately avoids structural_field_intensity as a routing key for now, since taxonomy_notes.md's early routing list is limited to semantic_state / dominant_operation / gradient / lifecycle_route / pass_state / method_family.

entries.title: Two Forces Hold an Even Line
entries.body: Neither side of this window's active signals is gaining ground on the other, and the total charge is holding steady rather than climbing. The strain is real but distributed evenly enough that nothing forces a decision on its own — the surrounding conditions carry the load rather than any single event.
entries.notes: semantic_state == frictional per _window_semantic_metrics(): conflicting operations without one side dominating. Plateau gradient rules out an imminent peak.

entries.title: Competing Directions Intensify
entries.body: The active signals in this window are not merely mismatched — they are pulling in directions that actively work against each other, and that opposition is still increasing rather than leveling off. Schedules, obligations, or standing commitments set on different tracks are the likely carriers of this kind of load.
entries.notes: semantic_state == opposed is the highest-conflict classification in _window_semantic_metrics(); rising gradient means the conflict has not yet crested.

entries.title: Instability Becomes the Steady Condition
entries.body: The dominant operation across this window's signals is disruption, but the signals agree with each other about it — this is not scattered interference, it is a consistent, reinforced pattern of disruption. Equipment, logistics, or scheduling systems under this kind of load tend to show repeated small failures rather than one large one.
entries.notes: Deliberate pairing of dominant_operation=disrupt with semantic_state=reinforcing: the signals agree on destabilizing, which reads as steady interference rather than one-off chaos.

entries.title: Contradictory Signals Share the Same Field
entries.body: No single operation is dominant here — the window's active signals do not agree closely enough to read as reinforcing, frictional, or fully opposed. The ambient condition is simply unsettled: public mood, group sentiment, or background noise that carries more than one current at once without resolving toward any of them.
entries.notes: semantic_state == mixed is the catch-all when constructive/dissolving mass and coalition size don't clear the thresholds for a cleaner read in _window_semantic_metrics().

entries.title: Accumulated Load Nears Its Limit
entries.body: This is not a new source of strain — it is the accumulated charge of a repeating pattern, now sitting at or near its recorded ceiling, and still reading as friction or direct opposition rather than agreement. Systems already running close to capacity are the ones most likely to show the load first.
entries.notes: Combines lifecycle_route == culminating (high memory_charge, plateau gradient) with a non-reinforcing semantic_state, for the specific texture of built-up strain that has not resolved into agreement.

entries.title: The Load Finds an Exit
entries.body: Dissolve is the dominant operation here, and the gradient is coming down rather than building — the pressure that was accumulating is starting to drain out through some available channel. This does not mean it is fully gone, only that the system has found somewhere for the charge to go.
entries.notes: dominant_operation == dissolve with releasing gradient: load actively decreasing, distinct from ts_residual_field which is a pass_state/lifecycle read rather than an operation read.
